name: OpenVibe.Food
description: OpenVibe.Food finds food banks, pantries and budget grocers near you from OpenStreetMap, plans meals for one person, a couple or a household with the shopping list and what it costs, shares the plan with your household, tells you what your cupboard can already make, and compares delivery: one search opens DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub and the other apps at once, with meal kits side by side. Next: a household chat with an AI member that knows your cupboards.

pillars.title: Food near you
pillars.text: Food banks, pantries, community fridges and budget grocers, with distance, address and hours.

pillars.title: A meal planner
pillars.text: One person, a couple or a household, up to fourteen days, with the shopping list and its cost.

pillars.title: Plan together
pillars.text: Share a saved plan with your household: everyone sees it and ticks the shopping list off as they buy.

pillars.title: A food list you can read
pillars.text: Nutrition per serving and per 100 g, the typical price band and the cheapest budget chain.

pillars.title: Cupboard recipes
pillars.text: Scan barcodes, or snap a shelf or a receipt, to fill your cupboard; it says what you can make and suggests recipes.

pillars.title: A recipe library
pillars.text: Budget recipes written by AI from the food list, each with what to buy and its typical cost; the ones a person checked are marked.

pillars.title: Delivery, compared
pillars.text: Search DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub, Seamless, Caviar and Instacart at once, and compare meal kits by tier.

faq.question: Is it free?
faq.answer: Yes. Searching for food and reading the food list need no account; a free OpenVibe account keeps your plans and your cupboard.

faq.question: Where do the food banks and stores come from?
faq.answer: From OpenStreetMap, the map anyone can edit, under the Open Database License. Every result is credited and links to its OpenStreetMap entry, and answers are cached for a week so OpenStreetMap is asked politely.

faq.question: Are the prices live?
faq.answer: No. The food list carries typical prices from budget chains, and every price says so.

faq.question: How does the meal planner work?
faq.answer: Tell it how many people, how many days and, if you like, a budget. It picks budget foods that cover each food group, splits the shopping by the cheapest store and lays out a menu for each day.

faq.question: Is the cupboard advice dietary advice?
faq.answer: No. It matches what you have against simple recipes written by OpenVibe and says which ones you can make now and which need one or two more things.

keywords: openvibe food, food bank near me, food pantry finder, budget grocery stores, meal planner, shopping list cost, recipes from your cupboard
